clue.text: See one plant after another surrounding seconds in charity store

indicators.note: to surround is to sit on both sides of something, so the two plants are placed either side of the letter for seconds

parts.note: thrift, or sea pink, is a coastal flowering plant
the hop is the climbing plant used in brewing
S is the abbreviation for seconds

explanation.surface: An invitation to look over one plant after another in a charity shop's stock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After another' puts the hop second; the two plants then sit either side of S.
explanation.definitionFit: A thrift shop is the American term for a shop selling donated secondhand goods to raise money for good causes.

clue.text: Unlikely to add up with unknown amount missing

indicators.note: something missing is absent, so the letter for the unknown amount is taken away

parts.note: to tally is to count up or total
Y is one of the algebraic letters standing for an unknown quantity

explanation.surface: Figures that will not add up because an unknown amount has gone missing.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition sense is the one in 'a tall story'.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall story or tall order is one that is hard to believe or improbable, so tall can mean unlikely.

clue.text: Checks about fans

parts.note: re means regarding or about
buffs are enthusiasts, as in film buffs

explanation.surface: Someone examining the fans, as on a ventilation inspection.
explanation.definitionFit: To rebuff is to repel or snub an advance, which checks or stops it in its tracks.

clue.text: In favour of suitable action in addition?

parts.note: to be for something is to favour it
good in the sense of fit or suitable
a measure is a course of action taken, as in drastic measures

explanation.surface: Backing an appropriate step, as a supporter might in a debate.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes something extra given beyond what is strictly required, so it means as a bonus or besides.

clue.text: Cross with sailor over rage

parts.note: an old salt is an experienced sailor
ire is anger

explanation.surface: An angry sailor, cross about a fit of temper.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' puts the sailor above the rage. 'Cross' looks like an adjective for angry but is a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A saltire is a diagonal X-shaped heraldic cross, as on the Scottish flag of St Andrew.

clue.text: Disgusting, old boy on stage

parts.note: OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil
the scene is the stage or setting of action

explanation.surface: An old man performing lewdly on stage, to the audience's disgust.
explanation.definitionFit: Obscene describes something offensive or repugnant to accepted decency, hence revolting or disgusting.

clue.text: Chances drop of Scotch after rum

indicators.note: after places the whisky's piece second, following the word for strange

parts.note: rum in its old sense of strange or peculiar

indicators.note: a drop is only a tiny taste, so just the opening letter of the drink is used

parts.note: the opening letter of the whisky

explanation.surface: A drinker weighing the chances of a whisky chaser following rum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rum' is not the spirit but the adjective meaning strange.
explanation.definitionFit: Odds are the betting ratios expressing likelihood, so they stand for chances or probabilities.

clue.text: Certificate envoy left unfinished

indicators.note: a job left unfinished lacks its end, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: a diplomat is an envoy representing a country abroad

explanation.surface: An envoy who has walked out before completing a qualification.
explanation.definitionFit: A diploma is a document awarded on completing a course, a certificate of qualification.

clue.text: Ruin gent, one she abused

indicators.note: something abused is mistreated and knocked about, so these words are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A woman mistreats a gentleman so badly she destroys him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ruin' reads as a verb but is the noun for an ancient remains.
explanation.definitionFit: Stonehenge is the prehistoric stone circle on Salisbury Plain, a famous ancient monument now partly fallen into ruin.

clue.text: Prince Edward, say, on manoeuvres with British Army Corps

parts.note: Prince Edward is an example of a royal, a member of the royal family
to engineer is to manoeuvre or contrive, so engineers means manoeuvres as a verb

explanation.surface: A prince out on military exercises alongside the British army.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Manoeuvres' suggests army exercises, but here it is the verb meaning contrives.
explanation.definitionFit: The Royal Engineers are the British Army's corps of military engineers, popularly called the Sappers.

clue.text: I, leaving African country, left enlightened

indicators.note: when one thing is leaving another it departs from it, so that letter is removed from the country's name

parts.note: Liberia is a country in West Africa
taken as written, the letter to remove
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: Someone who quit an African country and left as an enlightened person.
explanation.definitionFit: Liberal means open-minded and tolerant, free from prejudice, which is what an enlightened outlook is.

clue.text: Sign last of letters to CO about one in favour of retreating

indicators.note: the last of something is its end, so only the final letter of the word is kept

parts.note: the final letter of the word

indicators.note: about means around, so the abbreviation is placed on either side of the reversed phrase

parts.note: taken as written: CO is a commanding officer

indicators.note: retreating means going backwards, so the phrase about one in favour is read from right to left

parts.note: the Roman numeral one
pro means for or in favour of

explanation.surface: A soldier signs off the last of his letters to the commanding officer about a supporter who is withdrawing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One in favour of' is read in that order before being turned round, so the numeral ends up last inside the outer pair.
explanation.definitionFit: Scorpio is one of the twelve signs of the zodiac, the scorpion, for late October to November birthdays.

clue.text: Like a gypsy I'd boxed, a one-off possibly?

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters could be arranged another way than shown

parts.note: taken as written, apostrophe dropped
taken as written
taken as written, hyphen dropped

explanation.surface: A boxer recalls a single bout against a traveller.
explanation.definitionFit: A traveller who moves from place to place has no permanent home, the legal phrase for being without a settled address.

clue.text: Chancellor's quality town house?

parts.note: Gordon Brown was Britain's Chancellor of the Exchequer for ten years before becoming Prime Minister
tone is a characteristic quality, as of a voice

explanation.surface: Asking whether a politician's tone suits the townhouse he lives in.
explanation.walkthrough: The Chancellor of the Exchequer is Britain's finance minister; the question mark flags an American-style answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A brownstone is a terraced row house faced with reddish-brown sandstone, typical of New York streets.

clue.text: Some form of rise expected for the rest

indicators.note: a form of something is a version in a new shape, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
due means expected, as in a train due at noon

explanation.surface: A pay rise is anticipated for the rest of the staff.
explanation.definitionFit: A residue is whatever remains after part has been taken away, the remainder or leftover.

clue.text: Raise the Spanish girl round outskirts of Ascot

parts.note: el is the Spanish for the

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so the girl's name is wrapped about the kept letters

parts.note: Eve is a girl's name

indicators.note: the outskirts are the edges of a place, so only the first and last letters of the racecourse name are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters of the name

explanation.surface: A Spanish girl being lifted up at the edge of Ascot racecourse.
explanation.walkthrough: Ascot is a famous English racecourse in Berkshire.
explanation.definitionFit: To elevate is to lift something up to a higher position, a direct synonym of raise.

clue.text: Published account as western ceremony finished

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for western
a rite is a ceremony
up means over or finished, as in time is up

explanation.surface: A newspaper report on the end of a western ceremony.
explanation.definitionFit: A write-up is a written report or review appearing in a newspaper or magazine.

clue.text: Senseless, one point about one in charge

parts.note: the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: about means around, so the point is placed on either side of the second one

parts.note: a dot is a point
the Roman numeral one again
IC is the abbreviation for in charge

explanation.surface: A complaint that an argument about who should be in charge is pointless.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiotic means utterly stupid, without good sense or reason, so senseless is a near synonym.

clue.text: For every class act …

parts.note: per means for each, as in miles per hour
a form is a school class

explanation.surface: A school-play announcement: every class is to put on an act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Act' is the verb here; a form is the usual British school term for a year group or class.
explanation.definitionFit: To perform is to act out a role or entertain an audience on stage.

clue.text: Writing, a means of communication?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: putting one's name to a document
second meaning: using sign language with the hands

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark hints that the second meaning is not writing but talking with the hands.
explanation.definitionFit: Signing is both autographing a document and using a sign language such as BSL to converse with the deaf.

clue.text: Heartless creditor in modest bar

parts.note: shy means bashful or modest
to bar a door is to lock it

explanation.surface: A ruthless moneylender sitting quietly in a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bar' suggests a pub, but it is the verb meaning fasten.
explanation.definitionFit: Shylock is the moneylender in Shakespeare's Merchant of Venice who demands a pound of flesh as forfeit, so a byword for a merciless lender.

clue.text: King of Spain's daughter, young one

parts.note: an infant is a young child
a means one, as in a single thing

explanation.surface: Describing the Spanish king's daughter as a young one.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase echoes the nursery rhyme 'I had a little nut tree', where the King of Spain's daughter comes to visit.
explanation.definitionFit: Infanta is the title given to a daughter of a reigning Spanish or Portuguese monarch.

clue.text: Cheekily we frisk any miss for a potential weapon

indicators.note: to act cheekily is to behave impudently, taking liberties, so these words are taken liberties with and jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Security guards impudently searching a young woman for anything dangerous.
explanation.definitionFit: The multi-tool pocket knife has blades that could be used to harm someone, so it could serve as a weapon.

clue.text: Row in store

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a tier or line, as of oars or switches
second meaning: a stock or reserve kept for later, as of blood

explanation.walkthrough: 'Row in store' looks like a shop quarrel; the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: A bank can be a tier of keys or oars in a line, and also a reserve held for use, like a blood bank.

clue.text: Working with sailor, I circle lake

parts.note: on means functioning, as a machine is on
a tar is a sailor
taken as written
the letter O is circle-shaped

explanation.surface: A sailor's account of working his way around a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: Lake Ontario is the easternmost and smallest by area of North America's five Great Lakes.

clue.text: Find a canoe adrift round one part of the Pacific

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so the rearranged letters are wrapped about the numeral
a boat adrift drifts out of position, so these letters float into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Instructions to locate a drifting canoe somewhere in the Pacific.
explanation.definitionFit: Oceania is the region of islands across the central and southern Pacific, including Polynesia, Melanesia and Micronesia.

clue.text: What engravers do in Letchworth

indicators.note: in tells you the letters sit inside the place name

parts.note: letters two to five of the place name

explanation.surface: A question about the craftsmen working in a Hertfordshire town.
explanation.walkthrough: Letchworth is a garden city in Hertfordshire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Engravers cut designs into metal, and to etch is to incise a design, typically using acid.

clue.text: Stoker mostly at work aboard vessel with funnel

indicators.note: something aboard a ship is inside it, so the vessel's word is wrapped around the rest

parts.note: a smack is a small sailing fishing boat

indicators.note: letters at work are busy and moving about, so they come out rearranged
mostly means not all of it, so the final letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A ship's stoker labouring below decks on a steamer with a funnel.
explanation.definitionFit: A smokestack is a tall chimney carrying smoke away, the funnel of a steamship or factory.
